claim: AWS KMS supports sending data of up to 4 KB to be encrypted directly; envelope encryption offers performance benefits because only the much smaller data key goes over the network.
question: How much data can you send to AWS KMS to encrypt directly, and why use envelope encryption instead?

values.display: 4 KB
envelope encryption reduces the network load

qualifiers.scope: per request sent to AWS KMS for direct encryption

evidence.quote: While AWS KMS does support sending data up to 4 KB to be encrypted directly, envelope encryption can offer significant performance benefits.
Envelope encryption reduces the network load since only the request and delivery of the much smaller data key go over the network.

claim: In envelope encryption, AWS KMS generates data keys that encrypt data locally in the AWS service or your application; AWS KMS does not retain or manage the data keys.
question: Does AWS KMS keep the data keys it generates for envelope encryption?

values.display: Data keys are not retained or managed

evidence.quote: Under this method, AWS KMS generates data keys that are used to encrypt data locally in the AWS service or your application.
Data keys are not retained or managed by AWS KMS.

claim: Data is typically encrypted with AWS KMS in three ways: by calling the KMS APIs directly, by having AWS services encrypt it with data keys protected by your KMS keys, or with the AWS Encryption SDK inside your own applications, in AWS or not.
question: Where is data encrypted when you use AWS KMS?

values.display: three scenarios
whether they operate in AWS or not

evidence.quote: There are typically three scenarios for how data is encrypted using AWS KMS.
First, you can use AWS KMS APIs directly to encrypt and decrypt data using your KMS keys stored in the service.
In this case data is encrypted using data keys that are protected by your KMS keys.
Third, you can use the AWS Encryption SDK that is integrated with AWS KMS to perform encryption within your own applications, whether they operate in AWS or not.

claim: AWS KMS is integrated with most other AWS services; some encrypt data by default with keys owned and managed by the service, and some let you choose between managing the keys yourself and letting the service manage them.
question: Which AWS services integrate with AWS KMS, and who manages the keys they use?

values.display: integrated with most other AWS services
encrypted by default
choice of managing the keys yourself

evidence.quote: AWS KMS is seamlessly integrated with most other AWS services to make encrypting data in those services easier.
In some cases, data is encrypted by default using keys that are stored in AWS KMS but owned and managed by the AWS service in question.
Some services give you the choice of managing the keys yourself or allowing the service to manage the keys on your behalf.

grant permissions to other accounts and services

claim: AWS recommends customer managed keys created and stored in the KMS HSMs, because they offer the most flexibility, policy control, lifecycle management (including automatic and on-demand rotation for symmetric encryption keys) and complete auditability.

claim: AWS KMS supports rotation of imported keys through on-demand rotation; for keys in an external key store (XKS), you manage all key lifecycle events, including rotation, in your own key manager.

you manage all key lifecycle events including rotation

evidence.quote: AWS KMS also supports rotation for imported keys using on-demand rotation, and for keys stored in the external key store (XKS), you manage all key lifecycle events including rotation for external keys in your key manager.

claim: KMS key rotation is not supported for asymmetric keys, HMAC keys, or keys generated in a CloudHSM cluster through the KMS custom key store feature.

claim: With automatic rotation you do not have to re-encrypt your data: AWS KMS keeps previous versions of the key to decrypt data encrypted under an old version, and encrypts all new requests under the newest version.
question: Do you need to re-encrypt data after AWS KMS rotates a key automatically?

values.display: you don’t have to re-encrypt your data
keeps previous versions of keys

evidence.quote: If you choose to have AWS KMS automatically rotate keys, you don’t have to re-encrypt your data.
AWS KMS automatically keeps previous versions of keys to use for decryption of data encrypted under an old version of a key.

claim: If you rotate imported or custom key store keys manually, you may have to re-encrypt your data, depending on whether you keep old versions of the keys available.
question: Do you need to re-encrypt data after a manual rotation of an imported or custom key store key?

values.display: you may have to re-encrypt your data

evidence.quote: If you manually rotate your imported or custom key store keys, you may have to re-encrypt your data depending on whether you decide to keep old versions of keys available.

claim: You can cancel key deletion during the waiting period; while a key is scheduled for deletion it cannot be used until you cancel the deletion.

claim: For a KMS key with imported key material, you can delete the key material on demand without a waiting period, or set an expiration time when you import it; you can re-import the material later.
question: How can imported key material be removed from a KMS key, and how fast?

values.display: without a waiting period
define an expiration time

evidence.quote: First, you can delete your imported key material on demand without a waiting period.
Second, at the time of importing the key material into the AWS KMS key, you can define an expiration time for how long AWS can use your imported key material before it is deleted.
You can re-import your key material into the AWS KMS key if you need to use it again.
